pool.q: Why is the binary system used in digital electronics?
o: Binary numbers need no electricity at all

Ten voltage levels are hard to generate in hardware

only the first output is HIGH

pool.q: A JK flip-flop currently has Q = 0. After a clock pulse with J = 1, K = 0, what is Q?
pool.e: J = 1, K = 0 sets: Q becomes 1 (JK has no forbidden state: 1-1 toggles).

pool.q: A JK flip-flop currently has Q = 1. After a clock pulse with J = 0, K = 1, what is Q?
pool.e: J = 0, K = 1 resets: Q becomes 0 (JK has no forbidden state: 1-1 toggles).

pool.q: A JK flip-flop currently has Q = 1. After a clock pulse with J = 1, K = 1, what is Q?
pool.e: J = 1, K = 1 toggles: Q becomes 0 (JK has no forbidden state: 1-1 toggles).

pool.q: A JK flip-flop currently has Q = 0. After a clock pulse with J = 0, K = 0, what is Q?
pool.e: J = 0, K = 0 holds: Q becomes 0 (JK has no forbidden state: 1-1 toggles).

pool.q: A JK flip-flop currently has Q = 0. After a clock pulse with J = 1, K = 1, what is Q?
pool.e: J = 1, K = 1 toggles: Q becomes 1 (JK has no forbidden state: 1-1 toggles).

pool.q: A JK flip-flop currently has Q = 1. After a clock pulse with J = 0, K = 0, what is Q?
pool.e: J = 0, K = 0 holds: Q becomes 1 (JK has no forbidden state: 1-1 toggles).

pool.q: A 2-to-4 decoder has its enable line LOW. What happens at the outputs?
pool.e: Enable LOW → every output LOW; enable HIGH → the selected output goes HIGH.

pool.q: A 2-to-4 decoder has its enable line HIGH. What happens at the outputs?
pool.e: Enable LOW → every output LOW; enable HIGH → the selected output goes HIGH.

pool.q: In a CMOS inverter with the input LOW (0 V), which transistor conducts and what is the output?
o: The PMOS conducts and the NMOS is off; output ≈ 0 V
The NMOS conducts and the PMOS is off; output ≈ VDD
The PMOS conducts and the NMOS is off; output ≈ VDD
pool.e: A LOW input gives the PMOS VGS = −VDD (on) and the NMOS VGS = 0 (off), so the PMOS pulls the output up to VDD.

pool.q: Why does a CMOS inverter have almost zero static power?
o: In a steady state one transistor is always off, so there is no dc path from the supply to ground
The load resistor is very large so the current is tiny
The CMOS supply voltage is always zero
Both the NMOS and the PMOS always conduct a little
pool.e: Only while switching do both conduct briefly and the load capacitance charges/discharges: that is the dynamic power.

pool.q: A symmetric CMOS inverter has VDD = 3.3 V, VTN = 0.7 V, VTP = −0.7 V and KR = Kn/Kp = 1. What is the switching threshold VSP?
A symmetric CMOS inverter has VDD = 5 V, VTN = 1 V, VTP = −1 V and KR = Kn/Kp = 1. What is the switching threshold VSP?
A CMOS inverter has VDD = 2.5 V, VTN = 0.5 V, VTP = −0.5 V and KR = Kn/Kp = 4. What is the switching threshold VSP?
pool.e: √KR = 2 so VSP = (2.5 − 0.5 + 0.5·2)/(1 + 2) = 3/3 = 1.00 V. A larger KR means a stronger NMOS and a threshold below VDD/2. Common slip: leaving out the square root of KR.

pool.q: If Kn is increased (a stronger NMOS) with everything else unchanged, how does the CMOS inverter switching threshold VSP change?
o: VSP decreases (moves toward the low level)
VSP is unchanged because it depends only on VDD
VSP rises in proportion to Kn
pool.e: VSP = (VDD + VTP + VTN√KR)/(1 + √KR) falls as KR rises (when VTN < VDD + VTP).

pool.q: A CMOS inverter drives C = 0.5 pF at VDD = 2.5 V and switches at f = 100 MHz. What is the dynamic power P = C·V²·f?
pool.e: P = 0.5·10⁻¹² × 2.5² × 10⁸ = 312.5 μW. The power scales with the square of the supply voltage.

pool.q: If the supply VDD of a CMOS inverter is halved (C and f unchanged), how does the dynamic power change?
o: It falls by a factor of 2
It falls by a factor of 4
It falls by a factor of 8
pool.e: P = C·V²·f is proportional to V², so V → V/2 gives P → P/4.

pool.q: A CMOS gate has delays tPHL = 0.4 ns and tPLH = 0.6 ns. What is the average propagation delay τp?
A gate has an average power P = 312.5 μW and a propagation delay τp = 1 ns. What is the power–delay product (PDP = P·τp)?
When vIN equals exactly the switching threshold VSP of a CMOS inverter, what are the two transistors doing?
o: The NMOS is cut off and the PMOS is in the triode region
Both are in saturation and the output is switching steeply
Both are in the triode region
pool.e: VSP is defined where vIN = vOUT; the two saturation currents are equal there and the inverter gain is very large.

pool.q: An open-loop op-amp has V₊ = 2 mV and V₋ = 0, supplies of ±13 V and Aol = 10⁵. What is the output?
pool.e: Aol·(V₊ − V₋) = 10⁵ × 2 mV = 200 V is far beyond the supply, so the output saturates at the positive supply (comparator action).
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM01 Q1-35…1-38

pool.q: Which op-amp circuit bridges an analog signal to digital logic levels?
pool.e: The comparator has only two saturated output levels, which match logic HIGH/LOW.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM01 Q1-35…1-38

pool.q: A voltage follower built with an op-amp receives 3 V at its input. What are the output and the gain?
pool.e: The output is wired straight to the inverting input so Acl = 1 and in phase: Vout = Vin.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM01 Q1-35…1-38

pool.q: How many outputs does a decoder with 4 code inputs have?
pool.e: n code inputs give 2ⁿ outputs: 2⁴ = 16.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM01 (encoders, decoders)

pool.q: A 4→2 priority encoder has inputs D3 D2 D1 D0 = 0 1 0 1 (D3 has the highest priority). What is the output code?
pool.e: The priority encoder picks the highest-priority input that is HIGH: D2, so the code is 2 = 10₂.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM01 (encoders, decoders)

pool.q: A TTL gate has VOH = 2.4 V, VOL = 0.4 V, VIH = 2.0 V, VIL = 0.8 V. What is the high-level noise margin NMH?
A 5 V CMOS gate has VOH = 4.9 V, VOL = 0.1 V, VIH = 3.5 V, VIL = 1.5 V. What is the gate noise margin (the smaller of NMH and NML)?
pool.e: NMH = 4.9 − 3.5 = 1.4 V; NML = 1.5 − 0.1 = 1.4 V; the noise margin is 1.4 V.

pool.q: Which logic family has the lowest static power but is sensitive to static electricity (ESD)?
pool.e: CMOS draws almost no static current but its thin MOS gate is easily damaged by ESD (see module 09).
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM01 (TTL, CMOS)

pool.q: Which process transfers the circuit pattern onto the semiconductor wafer when an IC is made?
pool.e: The circuit is patterned onto the wafer by photolithography and chemical steps; flow soldering and hole plating belong to printed circuit boards.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM01 (IC manufacture)

pool.q: On which base material are integrated circuit chips made?
pool.e: ICs are built on thin semiconductor wafers that are polished, cleaned and tested.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM01 (IC manufacture)

pool.q: Besides higher speed, what usually comes with more transistors on a chip?
o: The chip no longer needs photolithography
Power consumption and heat also rise
pool.e: More switching transistors mean more dynamic power, so the heat must be removed.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM01 (IC manufacture)

pool.q: After fabrication and testing, what is done to the wafer to obtain individual integrated circuits?
o: It is cut into individual chips (dies)
pool.e: A wafer holds many identical circuits; after testing it is cut into separate chips.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM01 (IC manufacture)

pool.q: According to EASA, which of the following is part of making an integrated circuit on a wafer?
o: Polishing, cleaning and testing the wafer
Etching copper foil with ferric chloride to make PCB traces
pool.e: Chips are made on thin wafers that are polished, cleaned, patterned by photolithography and chemistry, then tested; etching copper with ferric chloride belongs to PCB making.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM01 (IC manufacture)

pool.q: What is a “chip” (die) in integrated-circuit fabrication?
o: A small piece cut from the wafer that holds one complete integrated circuit
A layer of copper on a circuit board
pool.e: A wafer holds many identical circuits; each piece cut out is a chip holding one integrated circuit.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM01 (IC manufacture)

pool.q: An encoder with 16 input lines (one HIGH at a time) needs how many output bits?
pool.e: 2ⁿ = 16 so n = log₂16 = 4 bits.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM01 (encoders, decoders)

pool.q: How many 3→8 decoders with an enable pin are needed to build a 4→16 decoder?
pool.e: 16 outputs / 8 outputs per decoder = 2 decoders; the most significant code bit selects which one is enabled.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM01 (encoders, decoders)

pool.q: An open-loop op-amp (±15 V supplies, Aol = 10⁵) has V₊ = 3.2 V and V₋ = 3.1 V. What is the output?
pool.e: Aol·(V₊ − V₋) = 10⁵ × 0.1 V = 10 kV is far beyond the supply, so the output saturates at +15 V.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM01 Q1-35…1-38

pool.q: A comparator has a 2 V reference on the inverting input and a 2.5 V signal on the noninverting input, ±12 V supplies. What is the output level?
pool.e: V₊ − V₋ = +0.5 V > 0 so the output saturates positive.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM01 Q1-35…1-38

pool.q: What is the decimal value of 101101₂ + 11011₂ (add in binary, then convert)?
pool.e: 101101₂ = 45 and 11011₂ = 27; 45 + 27 = 72 = 1001000₂. (A bitwise OR gives 63; subtracting gives 18.)
pool.s: Generated hard multi-step question – EASA M04 SM01; Jaeger 5e Ch.7

pool.q: The decimal number 59 written in BCD is
pool.e: BCD codes each digit: 5 = 0101, 9 = 1001. Plain binary 59 is 111011; 1010 is not a valid BCD code.
pool.s: Generated hard multi-step question – EASA M04 SM01; Jaeger 5e Ch.7

pool.q: A 4-bit ripple-carry adder adds 1011₂ and 0110₂. The sum bits S3S2S1S0 and the final carry out are
pool.e: 11 + 6 = 17 = 1 0001₂: low four bits 0001 and a carry out of 1 (the fifth bit).
pool.s: Generated hard multi-step question – EASA M04 SM01; Jaeger 5e Ch.7

pool.q: A JK flip-flop starts with Q = 0. Over four successive clock pulses with (J, K) = (1,0), (1,1), (0,0), (1,1), the sequence of Q after each pulse is
pool.e: (1,0) sets Q = 1; (1,1) toggles → 0; (0,0) holds → 0; (1,1) toggles → 1.
pool.s: Generated hard multi-step question – EASA M04 SM01; Jaeger 5e Ch.7

pool.q: A 3-bit binary counter (cascaded toggle flip-flops) starts at 000. After 13 clock pulses its state is
pool.e: The counter repeats every 2³ = 8 pulses: 13 mod 8 = 5 = 101₂ (13 = 1101₂, keep the three low bits).
pool.s: Generated hard multi-step question – EASA M04 SM01; Jaeger 5e Ch.7

pool.q: The expression NOT(A·B̄ + Ā·B) is equivalent to which gate?
pool.e: A·B̄ + Ā·B is XOR; the inverse of XOR is XNOR (output 1 when the inputs are equal). Truth table: 1, 0, 0, 1.
pool.s: Generated hard multi-step question – EASA M04 SM01; Jaeger 5e Ch.7

pool.q: A CMOS inverter has VDD = 3.3 V, VTN = 0.6 V, VTP = −0.8 V, Kn = 225 μA/V², Kp = 100 μA/V². What is the switching threshold VSP?
A CMOS chip has 10,000 gates, each loaded with C = 2 pF, VDD = 1.8 V, a 200 MHz clock and an activity factor (fraction of gates switching) of 10 %. What is the dynamic power P = α·N·C·V²·f?
pool.e: P = 0.1 × 10⁴ × 2·10⁻¹² × 1.8² × 2·10⁸ = 1.296 W. Ignoring the activity factor gives 12.96 W; forgetting to square V gives 0.72 W; counting a single gate gives 0.13 mW.

pool.q: Gate A (VOH = 4.8 V, VOL = 0.2 V) drives gate B (VIH = 3.2 V, VIL = 1.4 V). The largest noise tolerated on a line that is LOW and on one that is HIGH is
pool.e: NML = VIL − VOL = 1.4 − 0.2 = 1.2 V; NMH = VOH − VIH = 4.8 − 3.2 = 1.6 V (VO of the driving gate, VI of the receiving gate).

pool.q: What is the minimum number of 2→4 decoders with an enable pin needed to build a 4→16 decoder?
pool.e: One decoder (the two high bits) enables one of four more decoders (the two low bits): 1 + 4 = 5, giving 4 × 4 = 16 outputs.
pool.s: Generated hard multi-step question – EASA M04 SM01; Jaeger 5e Ch.7

pool.q: An integrated circuit (IC) op-amp has
pool.e: An op-amp has an inverting and a noninverting input and a single output.

pool.q: Which of the following characteristics does not necessarily apply to an op-amp?
pool.e: High gain, high input impedance and low output impedance define an op-amp; low power consumption is a feature of some devices only.

pool.q: A differential amplifier
o: has one input and one output
pool.e: The differential amplifier is the input stage of an op-amp and has two outputs, so both the first and the third statements hold.

pool.q: When an op-amp is operated in the single-ended differential mode,
o: one input is grounded and a signal is applied to the other
pool.e: Single-ended differential mode: one input grounded, the signal applied to the other input.

pool.q: In the double-ended differential mode,
o: only one supply voltage is used
a signal is applied between the two inputs
pool.e: In double-ended mode the source sits between the inverting and noninverting inputs.

pool.q: In the common mode,
o: an identical signal appears on both inputs
pool.e: Common mode means the same signal is applied to both inputs.

pool.q: Common-mode gain is
pool.e: A good op-amp rejects common-mode signals, so Acm is very small (much less than 1).

pool.q: If Aol = 3500 and Acm = 0.35, the CMRR is
pool.e: CMRR = Aol/Acm = 3500/0.35 = 10,000, and 20·log10(10,000) = 80 dB, so both the ratio and the dB value are correct (1225 = 3500·0.35 is the wrong operation).

pool.q: With zero volts on both inputs, an op-amp ideally should have an output equal to
pool.e: The difference of the inputs is zero, so the output is ideally zero (in practice offsets make it slightly nonzero).

pool.q: Of the values listed, the most realistic value for open-loop gain of an op-amp is
pool.e: Typical general-purpose op-amps have Aol of 100,000 to 200,000 (≈100–106 dB); 80 dB is only 10,000 and 1 or 2000 are far too low.

pool.q: A certain op-amp has bias currents of 50 μA and 49.3 μA. The input offset current is
pool.e: IOS = |I1 − I2| = |50 − 49.3| μA = 0.7 μA = 700 nA (99.3 μA is the sum, 49.65 μA the average).

pool.q: The output of a particular op-amp increases 8 V in 12 μs. The slew rate is
pool.e: Slew rate = ΔVout/Δt = 8 V / 12 μs = 0.667 V/μs (96 multiplies and 1.5 inverts the ratio).

pool.q: The purpose of offset nulling is to
pool.e: Nulling trims the internal imbalance so the output is 0 V when both inputs are 0 V; it does not change the input signals or the gain.

pool.q: The use of negative feedback
o: reduces the voltage gain of an op-amp
pool.e: Negative feedback lowers the gain from Aol to a stable closed-loop value and keeps the op-amp out of saturation, i.e. linear; oscillation comes from positive feedback.

pool.q: For an op-amp with negative feedback, the output is
o: fed back to the inverting input
fed back to the noninverting input
pool.e: Negative feedback returns part of the output to the inverting (−) input, opposing the input signal.

pool.q: A certain noninverting amplifier has an Ri of 1.0 kΩ and an Rf of 100 kΩ. The closed-loop gain is
pool.e: Acl(NI) = 1 + Rf/Ri = 1 + 100/1.0 = 101 (100 would be the inverting magnitude).

pool.q: If the feedback resistor in Question 16 is open, the voltage gain
pool.e: With Rf open there is no feedback, so the gain rises to the open-loop gain Aol and the output saturates.

pool.q: A certain inverting amplifier has a closed-loop gain of 25. The op-amp has an open-loop gain of 100,000. If another op-amp with an open-loop gain of 200,000 is substituted in the configuration, the closed-loop gain
pool.e: Closed-loop gain is set by the external resistors, Acl ≈ −Rf/Ri, independent of Aol. (Exactly it changes by only ≈0.003 %, which Floyd treats as no change.)

pool.q: A voltage-follower
pool.e: The follower connects the output straight to the inverting input: Acl = 1, in phase, no Rf or Ri.

pool.q: Negative feedback
o: increases the input impedance and the bandwidth
increases the input and output impedances
decreases the output impedance and the bandwidth
does not affect impedances or bandwidth
pool.e: In the noninverting configuration Zin rises, Zout falls and the bandwidth grows by (1 + B·Aol).

pool.q: Bias current compensation
pool.e: A resistor equal to Ri‖Rf in the other input makes the bias-current drops equal and cancels the output error.

pool.q: The midrange open-loop gain of an op-amp
o: extends from 0 Hz to the upper critical frequency
extends from the lower critical frequency to the upper critical frequency
rolls off at 20 dB/decade beginning at 0 Hz
pool.e: An op-amp is dc-coupled, so the midrange gain is flat from 0 Hz up to the upper critical frequency; the roll-off starts at that frequency, not at 0 Hz.

pool.q: The frequency at which the open-loop gain is equal to 1 is called
pool.e: By definition fT is the frequency where Aol = 1 (0 dB).

pool.q: Phase shift through an op-amp is caused by
pool.e: The internal stages act as RC lag circuits; each adds up to −90° of phase shift.

pool.q: Each RC circuit in an op-amp
o: causes the gain to roll off at −6 dB/octave
causes the gain to roll off at −20 dB/decade

Four: single, double, multi-layered and flexible boards

o: One: only the through hole technology with wire lead pins
Two: through hole and surface mount, without any plated holes
Three: through hole, plated through hole, surface mount
Four: through hole, plated hole, surface mount and wire wrap
pool.e: Through hole, plated through hole and surface mount.

pool.q: Which two materials are commonly used to make PCBs?
o: Epoxy-resin-impregnated paper and epoxy-resin-impregnated fibreglass cloth
Phenolic-bonded steel plate and ceramic-coated aluminium foil
Silicone-rubber sheet and polyethylene-coated copper mesh
Waxed cardboard and lacquered plywood laminated with tin

pool.q: In PCB manufacture, copper foil is bonded to the board surface by
pool.e: Copper foil is bonded in a heat press.

pool.q: In a single-layer board, the components are mounted
o: buried inside the board material between the layers
on the same side as the exposed copper traces
on the side opposite the copper traces
on both sides of the board at the same time
pool.e: Leads pass through holes to be soldered to the traces on the other side.

pool.q: What is the difference between non-plated and plated through holes?
o: Presence of copper inside the insulating board material
The diameter of the drilled hole in the insulating board material
The colour of the base board and of the printed silkscreen legend
The number of components that are mounted on the board surface
pool.e: Plated holes have less resistivity at the joint and give mechanical stiffness.

pool.q: Plated through holes provide
o: a lower manufacturing cost than non-plated holes in every case
higher resistivity at the joint with no extra mechanical strength
lower resistivity at the joint and some mechanical stiffness
no electrical connection but only a decorative copper ring
pool.e: Non-plated holes are less expensive and faster to make.

pool.q: Which is a disadvantage of surface mount technology?
o: Components may be mounted on only one side of the board
Fewer components can be placed on the same area of board
Components are harder to align and solder in place
The technique cannot be used on double-sided printed boards
pool.e: SMT allows more components on the same PCB, but alignment and soldering are harder.

pool.q: In surface mount technology the component leads
o: lie flat and are soldered onto copper pads on the same side
pass through drilled holes and are soldered on the opposite side
are replaced by long wires that are twisted onto the traces
are only glued to the board with adhesive, without any solder
pool.e: The pads give both an electrical connection and mechanical rigidity.

pool.q: In a Ball Grid Array (BGA) package the leads are replaced by
o: small solder balls on the bottom of the component
long flexible wire leads that bend over the package edge
thin metal clips that grip the edge of the circuit board
rows of pins on the top surface of the component body
pool.e: BGA gives higher pin density.

pool.q: What is needed to install or remove BGA components?
o: Special equipment instead of a simple soldering iron
only a pair of fine tweezers and a small soldering iron
a hand-held hammer and a cold chisel for each ball
nothing special, ordinary wire cutters are sufficient
pool.e: The solder balls are under the package.

pool.q: Which two automated soldering principles are used today?
o: Arc welding and resistance spot welding
Hand soldering and laser soldering only
pool.e: Flow for through-hole, reflow for surface mount.

pool.q: In flow soldering the board is
o: heated in a reflow oven after solder paste is printed on every pad
dipped in molten tin solder so solder rises through plated-through holes
clamped between two hot plates without any molten solder involved
hand-soldered one joint at a time by a technician with an iron
pool.e: Used for through-hole components.

pool.q: In reflow soldering, solder paste is applied to
o: the outer edges of the board
the top of the component bodies
pool.e: The paste is then melted in a reflow oven.

pool.q: Components are held in place before reflow by
pool.e: Pick-and-place then the reflow oven melts the paste.

pool.q: Multi-layer boards are joined electrically by

pool.q: A via is made conductive by
o: filling the hole completely with a block of non-conductive plastic
painting the hole walls with a thin layer of insulating varnish
electroplating or inserting a hollow rivet
leaving the drilled hole empty and uncoated inside the board

pool.q: Thermal vias are used to

carry heat away from power devices
raise the electrical resistance of traces

pool.q: Multi-layer PCBs are designed with computer software because of
o: their complexity and the precise registration of traces between layers
their very low component density and the absence of any registration needs
the lack of any copper layers that must be aligned with each other
their single-sided structure and the ease of hand-drawing the traces

excessive mechanical stiffness caused by the plated through holes
unintended capacitive and inductive coupling between layers
total loss of copper through repeated reflow soldering cycles
pool.e: Computer modelling is used to mitigate such issues.

pool.q: Why should PCB soldering repair generally not be done in the field?
o: Physical laws forbid heating a printed circuit board in service
It needs no tools at all, so it is considered too easy to do
It needs special equipment with precise heat control
Boards in the field cannot be removed, so repair is impossible
pool.e: Removable PCBs (LRMs) are replaced or repaired in an equipped shop.

pool.e: Removable PCBs allow replacement of defective units.

pool.e: Boards are often coated with a protective laminate substance.

pool.q: ESD damages a component by
o: excessive heat and/or breakdown of the dielectric material
slow corrosion of the lead wires by moisture in the air
magnetising the metal case so the parts attract dust
bleaching the colour code printed on the component body
pool.e: The charge dissipates to ground and damages the part in the process.

pool.q: Electrostatic induction occurs when
o: a charged object redistributes charges in another object
two wires at equal voltage touch and a current flows between them
a battery slowly loses its stored chemical charge to the air
a fuse melts and opens the circuit under heavy load current
pool.e: Example: a charged comb picks up paper.

pool.q: Which of these materials should be kept out of an ESD work area?
pool.e: Nylon, mylar, vinyl, rubber, mica, ceramics, fibreglass, wood, styrofoam and plastic store static.

pool.q: Technicians entering an ESD work area should wear
o: wool sweaters with rubber-soled shoes to keep the body insulated
nylon coveralls and plastic-heeled shoes for maximum comfort
ordinary clothes, provided the floor is covered with carpet
pool.e: If wearing a heel strap, the cord must run into the sock to touch the skin.

pool.q: Work-station mats should be connected to ground through a resistor of
pool.e: The resistor protects personnel if the ground becomes electrically live.

pool.q: Why is a 1 megohm resistor placed between the mat/strap and ground?
o: To protect personnel if the ground becomes electrically live
To raise the static charge so that the mat attracts more dust
To heat the mat slightly and keep its surface dry for longer
To supply the power needed to run the ionizer fan motor
pool.e: It limits the current through the person.

pool.q: The wrist strap must be worn
o: around the ankle and connected directly to the live mains earth
loosely over a sleeve and removed whenever the board is picked up
only during soldering and clipped to the bench frame afterwards
securely around the wrist at all times while seated at the work station
pool.e: It must contact the skin to dissipate charge.

pool.q: A green light on a grounding test station indicates
o: the floor in the work area is wet and unsafe to enter
the test station is switched off and not measuring anything
the wrist strap is broken and must be replaced right away
the wrist strap is worn properly and working
pool.e: The test station can also test footwear, heel straps and coil cords.

pool.q: Ionizers are used to
o: amplify any static voltage so it can be measured easily
raise the relative humidity so that metals do not corrode
cool the components after they have been soldered in place
neutralize charged insulators in the work environment
pool.e: An air stream containing positive and negative ions neutralizes the charged surface.

pool.q: Why is it not practical to control static simply by raising the humidity?
o: Water is a perfect insulator and would trap more charge inside
Humidity itself creates the static charge that damages the parts
Operator discomfort and metals would rust
Raising humidity is forbidden by every military standard in force
pool.e: Hence ionizers are used.

pool.q: A work-station ionizer is normally mounted about
o: directly on the floor under the bench
3 to 6 inches above the work area
10 feet above the middle of the room
pool.e: It produces a balanced ionization pattern of about 36 in × 48 in.

pool.q: ESD-sensitive components should be transported in
o: an ordinary plastic bag in a coat pocket
an open cardboard tray on a rolling bench
a polystyrene box left on the floor
pool.e: The container is stored on a grounded rack and touches the grounded mat at the work station.

pool.q: ESD-sensitive components should be packaged in
o: an ordinary clear plastic bag from the stock room
plain paper wrapping held with a rubber band
loose foam packing peanuts inside a cardboard box
pool.e: The laminated bag has a metalized outer layer, an insulation layer and an anti-static inner layer.

pool.q: A soldering iron used to install ESD-sensitive components should be
pool.e: Always use a grounded soldering iron.

pool.q: Before opening a protective container holding an ESD-sensitive part, a person should
o: discharge body charge with a grounded wrist strap
walk across a carpet to build up a charge on the clothing
touch a plastic tray so that any charge moves to the plastic
remove the wrist strap and rest the hands on the container
pool.e: Wear the strap first.

o: CMOS and EPROM, but not bipolar transistors
pool.e: Compare 300 V with the lowest thresholds: 300 ≥ 250 (CMOS) and 300 ≥ 100 (EPROM) so both are at risk; 300 < 380 so bipolar transistors are below their threshold. (The ranges span different parts of one family, so "at risk" does not mean "certain to fail".)

pool.q: How many times larger is the static voltage produced by walking on a carpet at 20 % relative humidity (up to 35,000 V) than at 65 % relative humidity (1,500 V)?
pool.e: 35,000 V ÷ 1,500 V = 23.3: dry air multiplies the charge by more than twenty, which is why humidity and conductive floors matter.

pool.q: A technician has walked across a carpet at 65 % humidity and carries about 1,500 V. Using the damage ranges in the text (bipolar 380–7,000 V, CMOS 250–3,000 V, EPROM from 100 V), which parts can he damage by touching them?
o: Bipolar transistors, CMOS devices and EPROMs
CMOS devices and EPROMs but not bipolar transistors
No type: 1,500 V is below every threshold
pool.e: 1,500 V is above the lowest damaging voltage of all three families (380 V, 250 V, 100 V), so all of them are at risk.

pool.q: A person carries only 200 V. Which of these parts can still be damaged (lowest damaging voltage: bipolar 380 V, CMOS 250 V, EPROM 100 V)?
pool.e: 200 V exceeds the 100 V of EPROMs but not the 250 V of CMOS or the 380 V of bipolar transistors.

pool.q: A device is damaged only by discharges of about 2,500 V or more. In MIL-STD-1686C it belongs to
o: Neither class: the standard stops at 1,000 V
pool.e: The standard recognizes two classes by sensitivity: Class I for 100 to 1,000 V and Class II for 1,001 to 4,000 V; 2,500 V falls in Class II (most components are in Class I).

pool.q: Most electronic components are in MIL-STD-1686C Class I. This means that
o: they are damaged only by induction, never by contact
they tolerate 1,001 to 4,000 V without damage
they need no ESD control at the work station
they can be damaged by discharges of only 100 to 1,000 V
pool.e: Class I covers the most sensitive items (100 to 1,000 V), and most components are in it, so ordinary handling voltages are enough to damage them.

pool.q: According to the definition, an electrostatic charge can pass from one body to another by
o: conduction only: a charge cannot act at a distance
convection in moving air or radiation as light
conduction through physical contact or induction from a field
induction only: contact discharges are harmless
pool.e: ESD is the transfer of charge between bodies at different potentials, caused by direct contact or induced by an electrostatic field.

pool.q: A charged component is suddenly grounded. What happens?
o: It is safely discharged: grounding never harms a component
The charge stays on the part because insulators cannot discharge
The charge flows to ground but the component can be damaged by excessive heat or dielectric breakdown
pool.e: The sudden discharge dissipates the charge to ground, but in the process the part is damaged by heat and/or breakdown of its internal dielectric.

pool.q: In the comb-and-paper example the comb is charged negative. The side of the paper closest to the comb becomes
o: neutral, because paper is an insulator
pool.e: Electrostatic induction redistributes charge: the near side is attracted to positive, the far side repelled to negative, so the paper is pulled to the comb.

pool.q: Why do newer components need stronger ESD precautions than older ones?
o: They are packaged only in plastic
They contain more metal that attracts charge
Shrinking geometries make them susceptible to lower discharge voltages
pool.e: As components get faster and more capable their geometries shrink, so they become susceptible to ever lower discharge voltages: the ESD problem is getting worse, not better.

pool.q: Which action increases the static charge on a technician the most?
o: Walking fast across an ordinary floor when the humidity is below 20 %
Sitting at the bench wearing a grounded wrist strap
Walking slowly on a conductively coated floor
pool.e: Friction builds the charge; it grows as humidity drops below 20 % and the faster the person walks, while conductive floors and a grounded strap let it leak away.

pool.q: Plastics produce charges of 5,000 to 10,000 V. Compared with the lowest damaging voltage of a CMOS device (250 V), such a charge is at least
pool.e: 5,000 V ÷ 250 V = 20 at the very least (10,000 V gives 40): a plastic item near a CMOS part is far above its damage level.

pool.q: What does the 1 MΩ resistor in the grounding path of a mat or wrist strap do if the ground becomes electrically live?
o: It ionizes the air around the work station
It drains the static charge faster than a direct wire
It limits the current through the person and so protects the personnel
It measures the charge on the wrist
pool.e: The resistor is required to protect personnel in the event the ground becomes electrically live: it keeps a fault current through the body small (230 V across 1 MΩ is only 0.23 mA).

pool.q: A technician uses a heel strap instead of conductive shoes. For it to work
o: the grounding cord must run into the sock to touch the skin
the cord must be wound around the outside of a rubber sole
no skin contact is needed because the shoe conducts
the strap must be worn on the wrist as well
pool.e: The charge must be able to leave the body, so the grounding cord has to make contact with the skin inside the sock.

pool.q: A static-dissipative mat must have a surface resistivity of 10⁵ to 10¹² ohms per square inch. Which value qualifies?
o: 10² Ω per square inch (as conductive as metal)
pool.e: Only 10⁸ lies inside the 10⁵ to 10¹² range: dissipative enough to bleed charge away without being a short circuit, and not an insulator that would store it.

pool.q: Besides giving a surface free of static charge, a conductive table-top mat must also
o: remove the static charge from conductive items placed on it
store the charge for later measurement
pool.e: The mat is connected through 1 MΩ to a common ground point so that charge on items resting on it drains away.

pool.q: A technician tests a wrist strap at the grounding test station and the green light does not come on. What should he conclude?
o: He may enter and test again later at the bench
The strap is fine: green only means the station has power
The strap is not worn properly or not working; fix or replace it before entering the controlled area
Only footwear needs to be tested, not straps
pool.e: All anti-static devices are tested before entering the controlled environment; green means the strap is worn properly and working as intended, so no green light means it is not.

pool.q: Besides wrist straps, a grounding test station can also be used to test
o: footwear, heel straps and coil cords
pool.e: The same station checks footwear, heel straps and coil cords, i.e. every personal grounding path.

pool.q: How does an ionizer neutralize a charged insulating surface?
o: It sprays water mist to raise the humidity to 100 %
It heats the surface until the charge evaporates
An air stream with positive and negative ions lets the surface attract the ions of opposite charge
It generates a strong magnetic field
pool.e: Positively or negatively charged surfaces attract ions of the opposite charge; once neutralized the surface stays so as long as the ion stream is present.

pool.q: A work-station ionizer is normally mounted 30 to 36 inches above the area to be controlled. In centimetres this is about
The ionization pattern of an overhead ionizer is about 36 inches wide by 48 inches long. Its area is about
pool.e: 36 in × 48 in = 1,728 in²; each in² is 6.45·10⁻⁴ m², so about 1.1 m² (a bench-sized area).

pool.q: Before handling sensitive components, how should a technician make sure the ionizer is working?
o: Touch a grounded rack with a bare hand
Use an electrostatic field meter to detect static charges in the work area
Check that the room is at 65 % humidity
pool.e: The text recommends an electrostatic field meter to be assured that the ionizer is functioning properly before sensitive parts are handled.

pool.q: Which type of ionizer is meant for periodic, localized cleaning?
pool.e: Air guns are the high-pressure, low-volume type for localized cleaning; the low-pressure, high-volume units hang over the work station and blow ionized air down on the area.

pool.q: A closed conductive container of ESD-sensitive parts is brought from its rack to the work station. When it arrives it must
o: be placed on a plastic tray
be opened at once on any desk
make contact with the grounded table mat
be wrapped in a nylon cloth
pool.e: The container is stored on a grounded rack and, at the bench, touches the grounded mat so its charge equalizes with ground before it is opened.

pool.q: Which sequence is correct for installing an ESD-sensitive part taken from a protective container?
o: Put on the grounded wrist strap to discharge the body, open the container, install with a grounded soldering iron
Open the container, then put on the wrist strap, then install with an ordinary soldering iron
Install with a grounded iron, then discharge the body, then open the container
Open the container, install, then test the wrist strap
pool.e: Charge on the body is discharged first (grounded strap), only then is the protective container opened, and a grounded soldering iron is used for installation.

pool.q: From the outside to the inside, an electrostatic-shielded conductive bag is made of
o: an anti-static layer, an insulation layer, then a metalized sheet
a metalized sheet or aluminum foil, an insulation layer, then an anti-static layer
an insulation layer, a metalized sheet, then an anti-static layer
a metalized sheet, an anti-static layer, then an insulation layer
pool.e: The bag is laminated: outer transparent metalized sheet or aluminum foil, a middle insulation layer and an inner anti-static layer that touches the part.

pool.q: Where must the warning signs for an ESD-controlled area be placed?
o: Outside the controlled area, so people are warned before they enter
pool.e: Signage is placed outside any ESD-controlled area to warn people that special precautions are needed before they go in.

pool.q: Which of these is NOT named in the text as an insulating material that stores static electricity and must be kept out of the work area?
pool.e: The list is nylon, mylar, vinyl, rubber, mica, ceramics, fiberglass, wood, styrofoam and plastic; copper is a conductor, and conductive materials are grounded instead.

pool.q: Which technology lets more components fit on the same PCB, and what is its drawback?
o: Through hole: both sides can be used, but it needs special equipment
Surface mount: both sides can be used, but alignment and soldering are harder
BGA: a simple iron is enough, but pin density is low
Plated through hole: the cheapest and quickest to make
pool.e: SMT parts sit on the trace side and on both faces, so the density is higher; the only disadvantage given is that SMT components are more difficult to align and solder.

pool.q: The text describes BGA packages as having
o: lower pin density and easy hand soldering
higher pin density, but they need special equipment instead of a simple soldering iron
leads that pass through plated holes
no solder because they are glued
pool.e: Solder balls under the component give more connections in less space; installing or removing them needs special equipment.

pool.q: Leaded components are inserted into holes and the board is dipped in molten solder. This is
pool.e: In flow soldering the board moves on a conveyor and is dipped in molten tin; the solder is drawn up through the plated-through holes to form the joints.

pool.q: Chip components are placed on solder-paste pads, held by an adhesive and heated in a controlled oven. This is
pool.e: Solder paste is applied to the copper pads, parts are picked and placed and held by adhesive, then a reflow oven melts the paste to form the electrical connection and mechanical bond.

pool.q: Which statement about non-plated and plated through holes is correct?
o: Plated and non-plated holes differ only in diameter
Non-plated holes are more expensive but conduct better
Non-plated holes are cheaper and quicker to make but give less conductivity and stiffness at the joint
Plated holes have more resistivity at the joint
pool.e: Copper inside the hole is what makes the difference: lower resistivity and some mechanical stiffness, at the price of a more expensive and slower process.

pool.q: A via must join layers 2 and 3 of a multi-layer board and be invisible from both outer surfaces. It is a
pool.e: A buried via connects internal layers without being exposed to either surface.

pool.q: A via starts on the top surface and stops at an inner layer without reaching the bottom surface. It is a
pool.e: A blind via is exposed to only one side of the board.

pool.q: A power transistor on a multi-layer board runs too hot. Which feature of the board helps carry its heat away?
o: A blind via to the top layer only
More solder balls under the part
pool.e: Thermal vias are used to carry heat away from power devices and are typically arranged in an array.

pool.q: Why is computer modelling used when designing high-frequency multi-layer boards?
o: To limit unintended capacitive and inductive coupling between the layers
To reduce the number of vias to zero
To avoid the need for copper traces
pool.e: As designs become more complex, unintended coupling mechanisms appear between layers, particularly at high frequency; modelling is used to mitigate them.

pool.q: Which order of the PCB manufacturing steps described in the text is correct?
o: Bond copper foil (heat press), print the pattern in etch-resistive ink, etch away the unwanted copper
Etch the copper, bond the foil, then print the ink pattern
Print the ink pattern, etch, then bond the copper foil
Etch the copper, print the ink pattern, then bond the foil
pool.e: The foil is bonded to the board in a heat press, the circuit pattern is applied with etch-resistive ink, and the chemical etch removes the copper not protected by the ink.

pool.q: After etching, what remains of the copper foil?
o: Only the pattern protected by the etch-resistive ink: the traces
Only the copper under the components
Nothing: the traces are added afterwards as wire
pool.e: The unwanted copper is etched away by a photosensitive chemical process (ammonium persulfate or ferric chloride), leaving only the conductive pathways called traces.

pool.q: A printed circuit board in an aircraft system is defective. What does the text recommend?
o: Scrape off the protective laminate and repair it on the aircraft
Re-solder the joints in the field with a simple iron
Replace the removable module (LRM) and repair the board in an equipped shop
Leave it: printed circuit boards cannot be repaired
pool.e: Soldering needs special equipment with precise heat control and should not be done in the field; Line Replaceable Modules allow replacement of defective units, with repair by knowledgeable technicians in an equipped shop.

pool.q: A velocity servo has equal summing resistors R2 = R3, a motor turning 10 rpm per volt of error and a tachometer giving 0.1 V per rpm. The control input is −9 V. What is the steady-state speed?
pool.e: At balance N = K·e and e = (Vin − Vtach)/2 with Vtach = t·N, so N = K·Vin/(2 + K·t) = 10×9/(2 + 1) = 30 rpm (error signal 3 V). (Book example: −9 V, 10 rpm/V, 0.1 V/rpm → 30 rpm, error −3 V.)

pool.q: In the same velocity servo (control −9 V, equal R2 = R3, 10 rpm/V motor, 0.1 V/rpm tachometer) what is the error signal at the very first instant, before the load moves?
pool.e: The tach output is 0, so the sum point is (−9 + 0)/2 = -4.5 V. (Book: −9 V → −4.5 V.)

pool.q: A velocity servo has equal summing resistors R2 = R3, a motor turning 10 rpm per volt of error and a tachometer giving 0.1 V per rpm. The control input is −6 V. What is the steady-state speed?
pool.e: At balance N = K·e and e = (Vin − Vtach)/2 with Vtach = t·N, so N = K·Vin/(2 + K·t) = 10×6/(2 + 1) = 20 rpm (error signal 2 V). (Book example: −9 V, 10 rpm/V, 0.1 V/rpm → 30 rpm, error −3 V.)

pool.q: In the same velocity servo (control −6 V, equal R2 = R3, 10 rpm/V motor, 0.1 V/rpm tachometer) what is the error signal at the very first instant, before the load moves?
pool.e: The tach output is 0, so the sum point is (−6 + 0)/2 = -3 V. (Book: −9 V → −4.5 V.)

pool.q: A velocity servo has equal summing resistors R2 = R3, a motor turning 10 rpm per volt of error and a tachometer giving 0.1 V per rpm. The control input is −12 V. What is the steady-state speed?
pool.e: At balance N = K·e and e = (Vin − Vtach)/2 with Vtach = t·N, so N = K·Vin/(2 + K·t) = 10×12/(2 + 1) = 40 rpm (error signal 4 V). (Book example: −9 V, 10 rpm/V, 0.1 V/rpm → 30 rpm, error −3 V.)

pool.q: In the same velocity servo (control −12 V, equal R2 = R3, 10 rpm/V motor, 0.1 V/rpm tachometer) what is the error signal at the very first instant, before the load moves?
pool.e: The tach output is 0, so the sum point is (−12 + 0)/2 = -6 V. (Book: −9 V → −4.5 V.)

pool.q: A velocity servo has equal summing resistors R2 = R3, a motor turning 10 rpm per volt of error and a tachometer giving 0.1 V per rpm. The control input is −15 V. What is the steady-state speed?
pool.e: At balance N = K·e and e = (Vin − Vtach)/2 with Vtach = t·N, so N = K·Vin/(2 + K·t) = 10×15/(2 + 1) = 50 rpm (error signal 5 V). (Book example: −9 V, 10 rpm/V, 0.1 V/rpm → 30 rpm, error −3 V.)

pool.q: A velocity servo has equal summing resistors R2 = R3, a motor turning 20 rpm per volt of error and a tachometer giving 0.05 V per rpm. The control input is −9 V. What is the steady-state speed?
pool.e: At balance N = K·e and e = (Vin − Vtach)/2 with Vtach = t·N, so N = K·Vin/(2 + K·t) = 20×9/(2 + 1) = 60 rpm (error signal 3 V). (Book example: −9 V, 10 rpm/V, 0.1 V/rpm → 30 rpm, error −3 V.)

pool.q: In the same velocity servo (control −9 V, equal R2 = R3, 20 rpm/V motor, 0.05 V/rpm tachometer) what is the error signal at the very first instant, before the load moves?
pool.e: The tach output is 0, so the sum point is (−9 + 0)/2 = -4.5 V. (Book: −9 V → −4.5 V.)

pool.q: A velocity servo has equal summing resistors R2 = R3, a motor turning 5 rpm per volt of error and a tachometer giving 0.2 V per rpm. The control input is −8 V. What is the steady-state speed?
pool.e: At balance N = K·e and e = (Vin − Vtach)/2 with Vtach = t·N, so N = K·Vin/(2 + K·t) = 5×8/(2 + 1) = 13.3 rpm (error signal 2.67 V). (Book example: −9 V, 10 rpm/V, 0.1 V/rpm → 30 rpm, error −3 V.)

pool.q: A velocity servo has equal summing resistors R2 = R3, a motor turning 10 rpm per volt of error and a tachometer giving 0.1 V per rpm. The control input is −10 V. What is the steady-state speed?
pool.e: At balance N = K·e and e = (Vin − Vtach)/2 with Vtach = t·N, so N = K·Vin/(2 + K·t) = 10×10/(2 + 1) = 33.3 rpm (error signal 3.33 V). (Book example: −9 V, 10 rpm/V, 0.1 V/rpm → 30 rpm, error −3 V.)

pool.q: In a dc position servo with equal summing resistors R2 = R3, the input wiper gives 8 V and the feedback wiper gives -2 V. What is the voltage at the sum point (error signal)?
pool.e: With equal resistors the sum point is the average: (8 + (-2))/2 = 3 V. The motor stops when it reaches 0 V, i.e. feedback = −input. (Book: +10 V and 0 V give +5 V.)

pool.q: In a dc position servo with equal summing resistors R2 = R3, the input wiper gives -6 V and the feedback wiper gives 2 V. What is the voltage at the sum point (error signal)?
pool.e: With equal resistors the sum point is the average: (-6 + (2))/2 = -2 V. The motor stops when it reaches 0 V, i.e. feedback = −input. (Book: +10 V and 0 V give +5 V.)

pool.q: In a dc position servo with equal summing resistors R2 = R3, the input wiper gives 12 V and the feedback wiper gives -4 V. What is the voltage at the sum point (error signal)?
pool.e: With equal resistors the sum point is the average: (12 + (-4))/2 = 4 V. The motor stops when it reaches 0 V, i.e. feedback = −input. (Book: +10 V and 0 V give +5 V.)

pool.q: A synchro has a 2.2:1 step-down from the rotor to a single stator coil. With 115 V on the rotor, what is the maximum voltage induced in one stator coil?
pool.e: V = 115/2.2 = 52.3 V at maximum magnetic coupling. (Book: 115 V → 52 V.)

pool.q: A synchro has a 2.2:1 step-down from the rotor to a single stator coil. With 26 V on the rotor, what is the maximum voltage induced in one stator coil?
pool.e: V = 26/2.2 = 11.8 V at maximum magnetic coupling. (Book: 115 V → 52 V.)

pool.q: A synchro has a 2.2:1 step-down from the rotor to a single stator coil. With 90 V on the rotor, what is the maximum voltage induced in one stator coil?
pool.e: V = 90/2.2 = 40.9 V at maximum magnetic coupling. (Book: 115 V → 52 V.)

pool.q: A synchro has a 2.2:1 step-down from the rotor to a single stator coil. With 57.5 V on the rotor, what is the maximum voltage induced in one stator coil?
pool.e: V = 57.5/2.2 = 26.1 V at maximum magnetic coupling. (Book: 115 V → 52 V.)

pool.q: A synchro has a 2.2:1 step-down from the rotor to a single stator coil. With 230 V on the rotor, what is the maximum voltage induced in one stator coil?
pool.e: V = 230/2.2 = 105 V at maximum magnetic coupling. (Book: 115 V → 52 V.)

pool.q: A servomechanism is an electric control system that
o: converts motion into heat for cooling purposes
stores energy in a spring and releases it slowly
produces motion or force from a low-energy input
replaces a hydraulic pump with a passive valve
pool.e: The amplified signal usually drives an electric or hydraulic motor.

pool.q: Servomechanisms are integral to which aircraft system?
o: The passenger cabin lighting circuits only
pool.e: They are also used in flight instruments, autothrottle and radar antennas.

pool.q: A conventional voltmeter is an example of
pool.e: It has no feedback, so its accuracy depends on spring tension, magnet strength and friction.

pool.q: In a closed-loop system the difference between input and output is driven to
o: the maximum value allowed by the amplifier
a fixed positive offset of one volt
pool.e: The output is continually compared with the input.

pool.q: Why are open-loop systems not used for automatic flight control?
o: They need more electrical power than closed-loop ones
It cannot tell if the setting was not reached
They cannot drive any electric motor at all
They are always heavier than synchro systems
pool.e: Bearing friction and wind load can prevent the commanded setting being reached.

pool.q: The error detector of a closed-loop system is known as the
pool.e: It computes the difference between the desired input and the measured state.

pool.q: In the potentiometer servo, the summing circuit is
o: a lamp that lights up when the servo reaches the null
a gear train that adds the shaft angles of two inputs
a capacitor bank that stores the error signal charge
a resistor network adding the two voltages
pool.e: It gives the difference signal to the amplifier.

pool.q: A gear train between the servomotor and the load is used to
o: reduce the error signal to zero at the summing point
increase the torque available to move the control surface
generate the reference voltage for the potentiometers
measure the surface angle electrically for the display
pool.e: The gear train amplifies the torque output.

pool.q: An LVDT is basically
o: a pair of capacitor plates with a moving dielectric sleeve
a single-turn coil with a fixed permanent magnet and a pointer
a transformer with two secondaries and a moving core
a resistor with a sliding brush driven by the control shaft
pool.e: The differential of the two secondary voltages is the feedback signal.

pool.q: When the LVDT armature is exactly midway between the two secondary coils, the output is
o: a dc voltage of one volt
maximum, because both coils are fully coupled
pool.e: The null position gives no output.

pool.q: What does an RVDT measure that an LVDT does not?
pool.e: An RVDT is basically a transformer measuring angular rather than linear motion.

pool.q: Why are variable-coupling transducers very stable?
o: They contain several sliding brushes that wear out slowly
Only an inductive link joins the coils
They are completely filled with oil to damp the vibration
Their permanent magnets never lose strength with ageing
pool.e: The only moving part is the core.

pool.q: A synchro system is a servomechanism used for
o: storing digital data in the flight computer memory
amplifying weak audio signals for the cockpit speakers
transmitting information from one point to another
generating high voltage for the ignition exciters
pool.e: A synchronous transmitter drives a synchronous receiver and indicator.

pool.q: The three most common synchro types are
o: DC autosyn, DC magnesyn and AC selsyn
DC selsyn, AC autosyn and AC magnesyn
pool.e: Selsyn is DC; autosyn and magnesyn are AC.

pool.q: Selsyn is an abbreviation of
pool.e: Aircraft with only DC power use the DC selsyn system.

pool.q: In a DC selsyn transmitter the resistance winding is tapped in three places
pool.e: The taps feed the three toroidal windings of the indicator motor.

pool.q: The damping device in a synchro receiver prevents
pool.e: It feeds back some of the signal, slowing the approach to the indication point.

pool.q: A magnasyn system uses rotors that are
pool.e: Autosyn rotors are electromagnets.

pool.q: Autosyn transmitters and receivers are identical and contain
o: single-phase AC rotors and three-phase stators
pool.e: The stators are not externally energised.

pool.q: In an AC synchro system, if transmitter and receiver are at the same shaft angle then
pool.e: The induced stator voltages are identical; a misalignment produces current and torque.

pool.q: The torque synchro is designed to
o: give a light torque output without additional servo components
drive heavy gun mounts directly from the amplifier output
produce a high-voltage dc output for the servo amplifier
measure the fuel quantity by comparing two capacitances
pool.e: It positions an indicator pointer or other small-torque device.

pool.q: In a control synchro system the control transformer (CT) produces
o: an error voltage proportional to the angle difference
a torque proportional to the angular sum of the TX and CT
a reference voltage equal to the supply, independent of angle
a dc voltage proportional to the speed of the servomotor
pool.e: The error signal is amplified to drive the servomotor.

pool.q: A torque differential transmitter (TDX) sits between
o: the amplifier and the servomotor of the control loop
a torque transmitter (TX) and a torque receiver (TR)
the power supply and the load of the indicator
two identical torque receivers in the same housing
pool.e: The TDX accepts two position inputs and outputs their sum or difference.

pool.q: Reversing the stator leads S1–S3 between the TX and TDX makes the TDX output
o: the product of the two positions
the sum of the two positions
pool.e: Without reversal it adds the inputs; reversed, it subtracts.

pool.q: The only construction difference between a TDR and a TDX is that the receiver has
o: a permanent-magnet rotor in place of the winding
a second stator winding wound on the same rotor
a damper preventing the rotor oscillating
an extra slip ring that carries a dc supply
pool.e: The TDR gives one mechanical output as the sum or difference of two electrical signals.

pool.q: A resolver has two stator windings placed
pool.e: Its outputs are sine and cosine of the rotor angle (Cartesian coordinates).

pool.q: Resolver signals are typically fed into
o: Phase-locked loops for the cockpit display backlighting only
Digital-to-Analog Converters (DAC) for the cabin audio system
Hydraulic servo valves for the landing gear actuators only
pool.e: Resolvers are considered the most robust angular-measurement devices.

pool.q: Inductance transmitters are used in
o: older instruments, acceleration sensors and air data computers
modern fuel-quantity systems in transport category aircraft
landing-gear lock switches and flap position indicators
the cabin entertainment and passenger address systems
pool.e: An E-shaped core with a pivoting I-bar varies the secondary voltages.

pool.q: In an E–I inductance transmitter the primary voltage is fed to
o: the centre limb of the E
pool.e: The upper and lower limbs carry the secondary windings.

pool.q: A capacitance transmitter is found most often in
o: autosyn heading indicators in the cockpit panel
landing-gear lock switches on the main gear legs
resolver angle encoders on the flap drive shafts
pool.e: The tank unit has two concentric plates a fixed distance apart.

pool.q: The capacitance of a fuel-tank probe changes because
o: the plate spacing between the plates varies with the fuel level
the plate area between the plates varies with the fuel/air ratio
the dielectric constant varies with the fuel/air ratio
the supply frequency applied to the plates varies with the fuel
pool.e: Capacitance depends on plate area, spacing and dielectric constant; only the last changes.

pool.q: Hunting in a servo occurs because
o: the load is too light to overcome the static friction
the amplifier has too little gain to drive the load
the motor’s momentum carries it past the null
the supply is ac instead of dc in the servo loop
pool.e: The error then reverses phase and the process repeats; oscillations usually die out.

pool.q: A servo can become unstable when
o: the servomotor stops at the null and holds the load steady
the oscillations are damped out by the generator feedback voltage
the follow-up voltage becomes exactly equal to the control voltage
oscillations grow in amplitude (e.g. reversed lead)
pool.e: Inadvertent lead reversal of the feedback signal is the example given.

pool.q: Damping with a generator feeds back a voltage proportional to
pool.e: The follow-up voltage is proportional to the error; the generator voltage to velocity.

pool.q: The degree of damping is controlled by
o: the number of poles of the synchro in the feedback path
the colour coding of the wiring in the servo loom
the generator feedback voltage in the summing circuit
the reference frequency of 400 Hz in the supply bus
pool.e: The summing circuit adds follow-up and generator voltages.

pool.q: A viscous damper consists of
o: a soft-iron core with two secondary coils and a movable armature
a pair of concentric capacitor plates and a sealed oil reservoir
a conducting drag cup and a magnet flywheel
a resistance winding with a rotating brush and a fixed magnet
pool.e: The viscous torque is proportional to the relative velocity.

pool.q: A viscous damper increases the motor’s inertia and
pool.e: It does not adversely affect starting voltage or stall torque.

pool.q: Which factor can affect servo stability apart from hunting?
o: The colour of the indicator dial
The length of the pilot’s checklist
pool.e: Also motor starting voltage, amplifier gain saturation and transient response.

pool.q: Which is one of the most common manufacturing defects in synchros?
pool.e: Ellipticity of the stator is a common geometric irregularity.

pool.q: Synchros are subject to which two types of defect error?
o: Inherent electrical errors and random manufacturing defects
Thermal errors and magnetic errors in the supply only
Software errors and calibration errors in the computer
Hydraulic errors and optical errors in the actuator
pool.e: Winding distribution is an inherent design limit.

pool.q: The word “synchro” is an abbreviation of
pool.e: A synchro operates like a variable transformer using electromagnetic induction.

pool.q: Torque-synchro systems are used to move
o: light loads such as dials and pointers
pool.e: Control-synchro systems move heavy loads.

pool.q: A synchro differs from a conventional transformer by having
o: a rotatable primary (rotor) and three stationary secondaries 120° apart
a fixed primary and a rotatable set of three secondaries 90° apart
two stationary primaries and a single rotatable secondary winding
three rotatable primaries and a single stationary secondary coil
pool.e: The magnetic field can therefore be rotated through 360°.

pool.q: With 115 V applied to the rotor and a 2.2:1 step-down to one stator coil, the maximum stator coil voltage is about
pool.e: 115/2.2 ≈ 52 V; it occurs at maximum magnetic coupling.

pool.q: Stator voltages of a synchro are always measured
o: at the common point of the three coils
pool.e: The common connection of the three stator coils is not physically accessible.

pool.q: In a control-synchro system the control transformer (CT) stator windings are considered the
o: secondary windings, with the rotor as the primary
primary windings, with the rotor as the secondary
pool.e: The CT output is taken from the R1–R2 rotor leads.

pool.q: When the CX and CT are both at 0°, the CT rotor is
o: parallel to the stator field with the maximum output voltage
perpendicular to the stator field (zero output)
locked by a brake so that no voltage can be induced
disconnected from the reference so it produces no signal
pool.e: This is the null; it is a peculiarity of the CT.

pool.q: The CT output voltage is called the error signal because it represents
o: the amount and direction of the CX–CT misalignment
the supply voltage and frequency delivered to the CX rotor winding
the speed and torque that the servomotor can deliver to the load
the temperature and humidity measured inside the synchro housing
pool.e: The amplified error signal moves the load.

pool.q: In the dc position servo, the error signal is the voltage at
o: the summing point of the input and feedback signals
the terminals of the motor driving the load shaft
the output of the power supply feeding the amplifier
the bearing that supports the output shaft of the load
pool.e: With equal R2 and R3, +10 V input and 0 V feedback give +5 V at the sum point.

pool.q: The position servo motor stops when
pool.e: The feedback equals the input with opposite polarity (+10 V and −10 V).

pool.q: In a velocity servo, when the loop is at correspondence (null)
o: the tachometer output is zero and the motor is idle
the error signal is zero and the load stops at once
an error signal still exists and the load moves
the motor reverses direction at every null crossing
pool.e: It is used where a constant speed is required, set by the error-signal level.

pool.q: The feedback device in a velocity servo is
o: a potentiometer on the load shaft
pool.e: In the example it produces 1 V for each 10 rpm.

pool.q: An acceleration servo uses as its feedback device
pool.e: It is widely used in rockets and missiles.

pool.q: Unequal summing resistors R2 and R3 in a velocity loop provide
o: extra damping of the gear train between motor and load
a scaling factor compensating tach output and motor input
a lower supply voltage for the servo amplifier stage
a position reference for the position servo loop
pool.e: The alternative is gearing between motor, load and tach.

pool.q: Increasing the servo amplifier gain reduces time lag but
o: removes the time lag entirely and so needs no damping at all
makes the load move more slowly but removes all oscillations
increases the risk of overshoot because of the load inertia
has no effect on the speed of response of the servo load
pool.e: The system must then be stabilised by damping.

pool.q: An overdamped servo system
o: is not bothered by oscillations but takes too long to synchronise
responds instantly but oscillates erratically around the null
has no restraining force and so overshoots many times
is unstable and its oscillations grow with every cycle
pool.e: An underdamped system responds instantly but is erratic around synchronisation.

pool.q: The simplest form of damping is
pool.e: Friction is applied to the output shaft, but it absorbs power as heat.

pool.q: A 12 V PWM pulse train with a 40 % duty cycle drives a servomotor. What is the average voltage?
pool.e: The average voltage = duty × V = 0.40 × 12 = 4.8 V.

pool.q: To make a PWM-driven servomotor run faster without changing the pulse amplitude, what must be done?
pool.e: A higher duty cycle means a higher average voltage on the motor, so it turns faster.

pool.q: An astable 555 with R1 = 1 kΩ, R2 = 10 kΩ supplies 12 V pulses to a servomotor through a driver. What are the duty cycle and the average pulse voltage?
pool.e: duty = (R1 + R2)/(R1 + 2R2) = 11/21 = 52.4 %; Vavg = 0.524 × 12 = 6.29 V. (Floyd has no 555 circuit that drives a servo; this is an application calculation.)

pool.q: Pulse-width modulation (PWM) controls a motor by changing which property of the pulses?
o: The pulse width (duty cycle) while the amplitude stays fixed
pool.e: PWM changes the average voltage through the pulse width, so the dissipation in the switching device is very low.

pool.q: How many stator windings does a resolver have and how far apart are they?
pool.e: The resolver has two stator windings 90° apart giving voltages ∝ sin θ and cos θ; it is the synchro that has three windings 120° apart.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM03 p.3.9

pool.q: The two windings of a resolver give voltages ∝ sin θ = 0.5 and ∝ cos θ = 0.866 (same scale factor). What is the rotor angle θ?
pool.e: θ = atan2(sin θ, cos θ) = atan2(0.5, 0.866) = 30°.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM03 p.3.9

pool.q: A resolver gives ∝ sin θ = +0.707 and ∝ cos θ = −0.707. What is the rotor angle (on the 0–360° circle)?
pool.e: Positive sine and negative cosine put the angle in the second quadrant: θ = atan2(0.707, −0.707) = 135° (not 45°). The two voltages identify the angle uniquely over the whole circle.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM03 p.3.9

pool.q: According to EASA, which angular-measurement device is the most robust and where do its sin/cos outputs usually go for the flight computers?
pool.e: The resolver is the most robust angular-measurement device; its sine and cosine voltages are digitised by an ADC for the flight computers.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM03 p.3.9

pool.q: The two secondaries of an LVDT (connected in series opposition) give 3.2 V and 1.8 V. What is the output voltage?
pool.e: The output is the difference of the secondary voltages: 3.2 − 1.8 = 1.4 V; its phase tells on which side the core has moved.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM03 p.3.4, 3.10

pool.q: An LVDT has a sensitivity of 0.2 V/mm in its linear range. What is the output when the core is 3 mm off centre?
pool.e: The output is linear in displacement: 0.2 V/mm × 3 mm = 0.6 V.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM03 p.3.4, 3.10

pool.q: The LVDT above outputs 1.5 V with a sensitivity of 0.2 V/mm (linear range). How far is the core from the centre?
pool.e: Displacement = output/sensitivity = 1.5 V / 0.2 V/mm = 7.5 mm.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM03 p.3.4, 3.10

pool.q: The LVDT core is exactly centred and each secondary gives 2.0 V. What is the differential output and what is this position called?
pool.e: The two voltages are equal and opposite so the difference is 0: the null position.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM03 p.3.4, 3.10

pool.q: A control transformer (CT) gives an error voltage of 0.15 V per degree of angular error (small-angle range). What error voltage does an 8° error give?
pool.e: The error voltage is proportional to the angular error: 0.15 V/° × 8° = 1.2 V.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM03 pp.3.7–3.10

pool.q: With a CT sensitivity of 0.12 V/°, the measured error voltage is 3.0 V. What is the angular error?
pool.e: Angular error = 3.0 V / 0.12 V/° = 25° (the phase of the voltage gives the direction).
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM03 pp.3.7–3.10

pool.q: A differential synchro (TDX) receives two input angles 40° and 25°. What is the output angle when wired normally and when two leads S1–S3 of one input are reversed?
pool.e: The TDX gives the sum of the two angles: 40° + 25° = 65°; reversing S1–S3 negates one angle, giving the difference 40° − 25° = 15°.
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM03 pp.3.7–3.10

pool.q: A resolver is excited with 10 V peak. At a rotor angle of 30°, what are the peak amplitudes of the sine and cosine outputs?
pool.e: Sine output = 10·sin 30° = 5.00 V; cosine output = 10·cos 30° = 8.66 V (windings 90° apart).
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM03 p.3.9

pool.q: A resolver gives ∝ sin θ = 0.866 and ∝ cos θ = 0.5. What is the rotor angle?
pool.s: Gap-fill (coverage loop) – EASA M04 SM03 p.3.9

pool.q: A 24 V PWM pulse train with a 25 % duty cycle drives a servomotor. What is the average voltage?
pool.e: The average voltage = duty × V = 0.25 × 24 = 6 V.

A velocity servo has a 15 V control voltage and two equal summing resistors (the summing-point voltage is the average of the control and tachometer voltages, e = (Vc − Vt)/2), a motor of 20 rpm per volt and a tachometer of 0.05 V per rpm. The steady speed and the error voltage at the summing point are
pool.e: Balance: ω = km·e and e = (Vc − kt·ω)/2 → ω = 20 × (15 − 0.05ω)/2 = 150 − 0.5ω → ω = 100 rpm; e = (15 − 5)/2 = 5 V (the error is not zero because a velocity servo needs an error to keep turning).
pool.s: Generated hard multi-step question – EASA M04 SM03; SERVOMECHANISM (sv)

pool.q: The servomotor needs at least 2 V to overcome static friction. The control transformer has a sensitivity of 0.15 V/° and the amplifier a gain of 40. The smallest static angular error of the servo loop is
pool.e: The error voltage needed = 2 V/40 = 0.05 V; angle = 0.05/0.15 = 0.333° (this is also why the deadband decides the accuracy).
pool.s: Generated hard multi-step question – EASA M04 SM03; SERVOMECHANISM (sv)

pool.q: A differential synchro TDX is connected so that its output angle = θ₁ + θ₂, where θ₁ = 135° is the angle of the transmitter TX feeding the TDX stator and θ₂ = 60° is the mechanical angle of the TDX rotor. If the S1 and S3 leads between the TX and the TDX are interchanged (θ₂ unchanged), the output angle becomes
pool.e: Interchanging S1–S3 reverses the sense of rotation, i.e. it changes the sign of θ₁ (checked with the stator voltages, S2 being the zero): output = −135° + 60° = −75° = 285°. 75° has the right size but the wrong sense; 195° is the unmodified wiring; −195° negates θ₂ as well.
pool.s: Generated hard multi-step question – SERVOMECHANISM §3.7–3.9 (S1–S3 reversal; TDX adds or subtracts by wiring)

pool.q: A synchro has a 115 V rotor with a 2.2:1 step-down to each stator coil. With the rotor shaft 60° from the axis of stator coil S1 (coil voltage ∝ cos of the offset), the rms voltage on coil S1 is
pool.e: Maximum = 115/2.2 = 52.3 V (the SERVOMECHANISM text uses 52 V); V = Vmax·cos 60° = 26.1 V (cos 60° = 0.5).
pool.s: Generated hard multi-step question – EASA M04 SM03; SERVOMECHANISM (sv)

pool.q: A servomotor turns at 3000 rpm through a 60:1 reduction gear train (losses neglected). The load-shaft speed and the torque multiplication are
pool.e: A 60:1 reduction divides the speed by 60 (3000/60 = 50 rpm) and multiplies the torque by 60 (power unchanged if losses are neglected): this is the gear train's job in a servo.
pool.s: Generated hard multi-step question – EASA M04 SM03; SERVOMECHANISM (sv)

pool.q: A fuel-tank capacitance probe has two fixed concentric cylindrical plates, an empty capacitance C0 = 100 pF, and a fuel dielectric constant of 2.1 (air 1.0). With the tank 60 % full by height the capacitance is about
pool.e: The fuel-covered and the air-filled parts are two capacitors in parallel: C = C0·[(1 − h) + εr·h] = 100 × (0.4 + 2.1 × 0.6) = 166 pF (plate area and spacing are fixed, only the dielectric changes).
pool.s: Generated hard multi-step question – EASA M04 SM03; SERVOMECHANISM (sv)
